transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ___. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... everyone keeps acting like I'm just making things up, or imagining it. But I know for a fact that the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house. And they follow me on my cleaning routes, too. I clean houses over in the Heights—beautiful homes, really, mostly hardwood floors which I actually prefer because vacuuming those thick, heavy rugs just absolutely kills my lower back. I've been doing this for twenty years, you know? I used to use this lemon polish on the wood, but one of my clients, Mrs. Higgins, she can't stand the smell of lemon, says it reminds her of a cheap motel. Can you believe that? People are just so particular about their houses. But anyway, they're watching me on my routes and at home to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. Which I am! I make his meals every single day, even when my hands are raw from scrubbing baseboards all afternoon. I just don't understand why they can't leave us be.
How certain are you that the hospital people and agency staff are actually watching your house?

I am absolutely certain. I mean, people keep acting like I'm imagining it, like I'm just making the whole thing up in my head, but I *know* they are. The hospital people, the agency folks—they're out there. They want to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband. Which, like I said, I am. I've always taken care of him, ever since we got married back in '88. We had this beautiful ceremony, actually, over at St. Jude's. My sister wore this hideous peach bridesmaid dress—she still complains about it to this day, says it washed her out completely. And she was right, it really did. She's always been a bit dramatic though, always making a fuss at family dinners about the turkey being too dry or the gravy being lumpy. But anyway, yes, I know for a fact they are watching us. They follow me on my routes, they watch the house... I'm not crazy, doctor. I know what I see.
Have you ever heard voices that other people could not hear?

Well, yes, actually. I do hear... well, it's a woman's voice. Even when the house is completely quiet and there's nobody else around, I hear her right near the kitchen window. She tells me to check the locks or move his pills around. It's as clear as day, like she's standing right next to me. The kitchen window, you know, it looks out over the Johnsons' backyard. They have this enormous oak tree that drops leaves all over our patio in the fall. I spend hours sweeping them up, and honestly, with my bad back from all the vacuuming, it's just exhausting. I told Mr. Johnson once that he really ought to trim those branches back, but he just smiled and waved me off. People can be so inconsiderate of their neighbors, don't you think? Like the time someone left their trash cans out for three whole days... but yes, that woman's voice, she's always right there by the window, telling me what to do with the pills and the locks.
Does the voice sound like it is coming from outside your head, as if someone is actually speaking in the room?

Yes, exactly. It's not in my head at all. It's like she's standing right there, right by the kitchen window, speaking out loud just like you and me. I can hear her clear as day telling me to check the locks or move his pills around. It's funny you ask about it sounding like it's in the room, because my husband's hearing has gotten so bad lately he wouldn't know if someone was shouting right next to him. We were at the grocery store last Tuesday—the one on 4th Street, not the big one out by the highway, because the big one always has those terrible squeaky carts—and the cashier asked him three times if he wanted his receipt. Three times! I had to elbow him in the ribs just to get his attention. He used to have perfect hearing, you know. When he worked at the auto plant, he could tell what was wrong with an engine just by listening to it hum. They don't make cars like that anymore, all computers now. If something breaks, you can't just open the hood and fix it yourself. But anyway, yes, the woman's voice is definitely outside my head, right there in the kitchen with me.
Have there been times when the voices and beliefs happened only when your mood was very high or very low?

Well, no, not really. I mean, they're just always there. There was this one time, a quieter spell for several weeks, where I was sleeping a lot more and not rushing around cleaning houses nearly as much. I just felt so drained, you know? But even then, I still heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window, and I still knew the agency was out there watching us. Speaking of cleaning, I had to drop one of my regular clients during that time—Mrs. Higgins. Oh, her house was always a disaster. She collects those little porcelain figurines, hundreds of them, all over the living room. Dusting them is a nightmare. I swear, she buys a new one every week from that antique shop downtown. The one with the green awning? They have lovely things, but the owner is so pushy. He tried to sell me a brass lamp once that looked like it belonged in a haunted house. I told him, "Where on earth would I put that?" My husband would trip over the cord in a heartbeat. But yes, even when I was exhausted and sleeping all the time, the voice and the agency people were still there. They don't take a break just because I'm tired.
How long have you been hearing the woman’s voice and believing that people are watching you like this?

Well, let me think... it's been about 11 months now that the voice and the feeling of them watching us has been going on. I know it's been 11 months because it started right around the time I had to buy a new vacuum cleaner for my housekeeping jobs. The motor on my old one just completely burned out right in the middle of a shift. It smelled like burning rubber all over Mrs. Gable's living room! I was so embarrassed. I had to run right out to the big store on the highway and buy a new one that same afternoon. I ended up getting this purple one with a special attachment for pet hair, which is honestly an absolute lifesaver because Mrs. Gable has two of those fluffy white cats. Persian cats, I think they're called? They shed everywhere. You just look at them and fur floats into the air. I spend half my morning just trying to get the hair off her dark blue velvet sofa. Who buys a velvet sofa when they have cats, anyway? It just doesn't make any sense to me. People really don't think ahead when they decorate. Like my sister, she bought a pure white rug for her front entryway, and with all the mud we get in the spring, it was ruined in a week. But anyway, yes, it's been about 11 months since the voice and the watching started.
During the past 11 months, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you were depressed or very high in mood, and the voice and watching were present only during that time?

Well, I don't know about *only* during that time, but I definitely had them when my mood was just... up in the clouds, I guess you'd say. There were a few weeks where I barely slept a wink, maybe two hours a night, and I was just running everywhere. I'd go from cleaning three houses in a row straight over to the church to organize the pantry, and the whole time, that woman's voice was right there with me, and I just *knew* they were tracking the routes I was taking around town. Speaking of the church pantry, you wouldn't believe the things people donate. Last month, someone dropped off six cans of cranberry sauce that expired in 2018! I mean, who keeps cranberry sauce that long? And they just toss it in the donation bin like they're doing some grand favor. I had to throw the whole lot out. Father Thomas hates wasting food, but I told him, "Father, we can't be giving people botulism for the holidays." He agreed, of course. He's such a sweet man, but he really doesn't know the first thing about organizing a kitchen. He keeps the flour right next to the sink! It's a disaster waiting to happen. But yes, during those weeks when I had all that energy and no sleep, the voice and the tracking were definitely happening right along with it.
Have there also been times over the past 11 months when the voice and the feeling that people were watching you were present even though you were not depressed, very high, or not sleeping much?

Well, yes, actually, I think I mentioned it earlier. There was that quieter spell, you know? It lasted for several weeks where I wasn't running around like a chicken with its head cut off, and I was actually sleeping a lot more. I wasn't rushing from house to house cleaning nearly as much. But even during that quieter time, when I felt so drained, I still heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window, and I still knew the agency was out there watching us. They never stop. It's like my neighbor, Mr. Henderson, he never stops mowing his lawn. I swear, he's out there three times a week with that loud gas mower. And he always does it right when I'm trying to watch my afternoon shows. It's just so inconsiderate. I don't understand why people can't just use a push mower, or at least wait until the evening. His grass isn't even that long! He just likes the noise, I think. He also leaves his garbage cans out by the curb for three days after pickup. It drives the neighborhood association crazy. They send him letters, but he just ignores them. Anyway, yes, even when I wasn't full of energy or depressed, the voice and the watching were still there.
Have you noticed any other unusual experiences, like feeling that your thoughts are being broadcast, controlled, or inserted by someone else?

Well, no... I don't think so. My thoughts are just my own. I mean, nobody is putting them in my head or broadcasting them on the radio or anything like that. Mostly I'm just thinking about my schedule, or what I need to pick up at the store for my next shift. 

Like just yesterday, I was thinking about how I need to get more of that lemon wood polish. The store brand, not the name brand. Though, honestly, they changed the formula on the name brand recently, which is why I switched. The bottle looks exactly the same, but the plastic cap is a slightly lighter yellow now, and I swear to you, it leaves this awful cloudy streak on mahogany. I used it on Mrs. Gable's dining table last week and it took me an extra twenty minutes just to buff it out with a microfiber cloth. And time is money in my line of work! If I spend an extra twenty minutes at every house, I'll never get home in time to watch my evening shows. 

I love watching Jeopardy while I eat my dinner. It's just a nice routine. Though it really hasn't been the same since Alex Trebek passed away, bless his heart. He was such a sharp dresser. Always had those perfectly tailored suits. You just don't see men dressing like that anymore, do you? Everyone is so casual nowadays, wearing sweatpants to the grocery store like they just rolled right out of bed. It's a shame, people used to take pride in how they presented themselves in public. My mother would have never let us out of the house in sweatpants. 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, about my thoughts. No, nothing unusual like that, just my regular thinking.
Over the past 11 months, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Depressed? Like, sad all the time? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I have my moments where I feel a bit worn out, but I've never been down in the dumps for weeks on end. Mostly I just keep moving. You have to, right? If you stop, the dust just settles. 

And speaking of dust, you wouldn't believe the amount of dust that accumulates on ceiling fan blades. It's like people just forget they exist up there! I was at the Miller house on Tuesday, and I don't think they've dusted their bedroom fan since the Bush administration. I had to get the stepladder out—and let me tell you, my knees aren't what they used to be for climbing up and down ladders. I should probably start taking that glucosamine supplement my sister keeps telling me about. She swears by it, says she can practically do jumping jacks now. But she also buys all those vitamins from that mail-order catalog, the one with the really flimsy paper? I always tell her she's just paying for expensive pee, but she won't listen. She never listens. Even when we were kids, she'd just dig her heels in. 

But no, to answer your question, I haven't really had any long stretches of feeling depressed like that. Just busy, mostly.
Have there been any times when the voice and the belief that people were watching you were happening even though your mood felt completely normal?

I think I might have mentioned this just a little bit ago, didn't I? About that quieter spell? Yes, there were several weeks where my mood was just... normal. I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't rushing around cleaning like a madwoman, just feeling regular. But yes, even during that time, I still heard that woman's voice right by the kitchen window, and I still firmly believed the agency was out there watching us. They don't take a break just because I do. 

And you know, speaking of that kitchen window, I really need to wash the glass on it. The rain we had last weekend left all these awful hard water spots. Some people say you should use white vinegar and old newspaper to clean windows so they don't streak, but I'll tell you what, the newspaper ink just gets all over your hands. I tried it once on these beautiful French doors at the Peterson house, and my fingers were pitch black by the time I finished the living room. I had to scrub them with Dawn dish soap for ten minutes, and that just ruins your cuticles. It dries your skin out so terribly. 

I actually had to go out and buy this special almond oil hand cream just to fix my hands, but the pump on the bottle is so cheap. It always stops working when there's still a good inch of lotion left at the bottom. You pump and pump and nothing comes out! It just makes you so mad, the way they manufacture things these days to make you throw it away and buy a new one before it's even empty. I usually end up cutting the plastic bottle open with a pair of kitchen shears just to scoop the rest out. 

But anyway, yes, to answer your question, even when I was feeling totally normal and sleeping fine, the voice and the watching were absolutely still happening.
Have you become more withdrawn from other people or lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Withdrawn? No, I wouldn't say that. I still see my clients every week, and I talk to my sister on the phone, even if she does drive me up the wall with her catalog vitamins. I haven't lost interest in my shows or anything. 

Speaking of my shows, they moved the time slot for Wheel of Fortune in my area, and it completely threw off my whole evening routine. It used to be right after the local news, perfectly timed for when I sit down with my dinner, but now they've swapped it with some syndicated sitcom from the nineties. I don't know who makes these decisions at the network, but they clearly don't think about the people who actually watch television. My neighbor, Mrs. Higgins—she's the one with the terrible rhododendrons that always drop leaves in my driveway—she actually called the station to complain. Can you imagine? Waiting on hold for twenty minutes just to yell at some poor intern about a game show. 

Though I will say, those rhododendrons are a menace. I spend half my Saturday morning just sweeping the driveway because if it rains, those leaves turn to absolute mush, and they stain the concrete. I bought this heavy-duty push broom from the hardware store, the one with the stiff bristles, but the handle is just a fraction too short. It makes my lower back ache if I use it for more than ten minutes. I should probably just get a leaf blower, but the gas ones are so loud and they smell terrible, and the battery ones never hold a charge long enough to finish the job. 

But no, I'm still doing all the things I usually do. Not withdrawn at all.
Have there ever been at least two weeks when the voice and the feeling that people were watching you were present even though you were not having any depression or unusually high mood at all?

I feel like we just talked about this, didn't we? Yes, like I was saying before, there was that quieter spell for several weeks. My mood was completely normal—I wasn't feeling down, and I wasn't having one of those spells where I'm rushing around cleaning everything in sight. I was actually sleeping a lot more, getting a solid eight hours, which is rare for me. But even with my mood being completely fine, I still heard that woman's voice right by the kitchen window, and I still knew for a fact that the agency was out there watching us. 

And you know, speaking of getting a good night's sleep, I had to buy a new mattress pad last month because my old one got a tear in it. I went to that big department store out by the highway, the one with the escalators that always seem to be broken. I swear, every time I go there, there's an "out of order" sign. How hard is it to fix an escalator? It's just stairs that move! Anyway, I bought this quilted mattress pad that said it was "cooling," but let me tell you, it does the exact opposite. It traps all the body heat. I wake up in the middle of the night feeling like I'm in a sauna. 

I even tried changing my sheets to those 100% Egyptian cotton ones. They're supposed to be breathable, but they wrinkle so terribly in the dryer. If you don't take them out the exact second the buzzer goes off, they look like a crumpled-up paper bag. And ironing sheets? Who has time for that? I know a lady whose house I clean, Mrs. Gable, she actually pays a service to come and iron her bedsheets. Can you imagine having that kind of money? Just to sleep on smooth cotton. She has this tiny little lap dog, too, a Pomeranian, I think. It just yaps and yaps the entire time I'm trying to vacuum the baseboards. 

But yes, to get back to what you asked, even when I wasn't having any mood issues at all, the voice and the feeling of being watched were definitely still there.
Have you had any time when the voice was present but the belief that people were watching you was not?

No, I don't think so. They always seem to happen together. If I hear her talking by the window, I know they're out there watching. They just go together, like... well, like bleach and ammonia, which you should never mix, by the way! 

I had a girl working with me once at a house in the heights—young thing, barely out of high school, didn't know a thing about proper housekeeping. She thought she'd save time by mixing the toilet bowl cleaner with the floor bleach in the master bathroom, and the fumes were just awful. We had to open every window in the house and stand out on the lawn for an hour. The homeowner's husband came back from his golf game right in the middle of it. He was wearing these bright plaid shorts, the kind that just hurt your eyes to look at. I don't understand why men think they can wear neon colors just because they're on a golf course. My ex-husband used to do the same thing, bought this awful salmon-colored polo shirt that he insisted was "coral." It clashed terribly with his complexion. 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, the voice. No, I've never had one without the other. If the voice is there, the watching is definitely there too.
Have you ever gone for at least two weeks when you were hearing the voice or believing you were being watched, but you were not having any manic symptoms at all?

I... didn't I just say this? I feel like we're going in circles here, Doctor. But yes, like I told you just a minute ago, there was that quiet spell for several weeks. I wasn't rushing around cleaning everything in sight or feeling all wound up, and I was actually sleeping a lot more. But even with all that calmness, I still heard that woman's voice right by the kitchen window, and I knew the agency was out there watching us. 

Speaking of the kitchen window, I really need to get someone to look at the caulking around the frame. It's starting to peel away, and when the wind blows from the east, you can feel a distinct draft right over the sink. I noticed it when I was washing my good china last week. I only bring out the good china for special occasions, but I decided to use it just for myself on Tuesday because, well, why not? But the draft was freezing my hands. I tried to buy some of that silicone sealant at the hardware store, but the tubes are impossible to squeeze if you don't have one of those metal caulking guns. I bought a cheap plastic one once, and it snapped right in half the second I put pressure on the trigger. Just completely useless. They make everything out of cheap plastic these days, don't they? 

My vacuum cleaner is the same way. The attachments are all plastic, and the little clip that holds the crevice tool broke off months ago. Now I have to carry the tool in my apron pocket when I clean my clients' houses. It pokes me in the ribs every time I bend over to dust a coffee table. 

But yes, to answer your question again, the voice and the watching were definitely there even when I wasn't feeling all sped up or manic, or whatever you want to call it.
Do people ever tell you that your speech gets hard to follow or jumps from one idea to another in a way that doesn’t make sense?

Well, yes, actually. I've had a few people mention that lately. When I try to explain what's happening, you know, with the agency or just my day, the words just sort of run together. I'll start talking about my husband's heart pills, and then somehow I'm on about the church schedule, and then the numbers on my client list for the week. And they just look at me and say they can't follow what I'm saying. 

Speaking of the church schedule, they changed the time for the Sunday bake sale without telling anyone. I showed up at nine with two dozen of my lemon bars, and the hall was completely locked. The janitor, Mr. Henderson, finally let me in, but he was grumbling the whole time about how he was supposed to have the morning off to go fishing. He has this old aluminum boat that he's constantly patching up. I think he spends more time fixing the boat than actually putting it in the water. He uses this marine epoxy that smells awful, like rotten eggs and vinegar. 

I bought some vinegar last week, actually, the big gallon jug, because it's the only thing that really gets the hard water stains off the glass shower doors at Mrs. Gable's house. You have to mix it with a little Dawn dish soap, the blue kind, not the green kind. The green kind smells like fake apples and gives me a headache. But you spray it on and let it sit, and it just melts the soap scum right off. 

But anyway, yes, people do tell me they can't understand me sometimes because my thoughts just jump all over the place.
Have these experiences with the voice and the feeling that people are watching you been going on continuously for at least six months?

Well, let me think... yes, it's been about 11 months now. Almost a full year of that woman's voice and knowing they're watching us. It started right around the time I was doing the spring cleaning at the Miller estate. 

Mrs. Miller had me washing all the baseboards in that massive house, and let me tell you, my knees were just screaming by the end of it. I had to buy these special gel knee pads from the garden center, the kind that strap around the back of your leg. But the straps always pinch right behind the knee if you wear shorts. I told my daughter she shouldn't wear shorts when she gardens either, because of the ticks. She lives out in the country now, got this little place with a wraparound porch. She painted the porch ceiling this light blue color—haint blue, they call it. Supposed to keep the wasps away, or maybe it's spirits, I can't remember. But she still gets mud daubers building nests right in the corners of the eaves. 

I hate mud daubers. You knock their nests down with a broom, and all these paralyzed spiders fall out. It's just horrifying. I use a special extension duster for my clients' high ceilings so I don't have to get too close to any bugs. The duster has a microfiber head that you can just pop in the washing machine, which is so much better than those old feather dusters that just push the dirt around. 

But yes, to answer your question, it's been about 11 months of all this going on.
Have you ever had a time when the voice or the belief that people were watching you was present for at least two weeks while you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?

I feel like we just talked about this, Doctor. Are you testing my memory? But yes, like I said before, there was a quieter spell for several weeks. I wasn't rushing around cleaning everything in sight, and I wasn't feeling down in the dumps either, you know? I was sleeping a lot more, actually. But even with all that calmness, I still heard that woman's voice right by the kitchen window, and I knew the agency was out there watching us. 

Speaking of sleeping more, I had to buy a new mattress pad because my old one got a tear right down the middle. I went to that big department store out by the highway, the one with the huge parking lot that always has those seagulls circling around. I don't know why seagulls hang out in parking lots so far from the ocean. They just sit on the light poles and squawk at people pushing their carts. I had a cart with a wonky wheel, of course. It kept pulling to the left, and I ended up bumping into a display of those scented pinecones they put out for the holidays. 

They smell so strong, those pinecones. Cinnamon and apple and I don't know what else. It gives me a terrible headache. I prefer natural scents, like lavender. I keep little sachets of dried lavender in my linen closet to keep the moths away. My grandmother taught me that. She used to grow huge bushes of it in her front yard, right next to the hydrangeas. Her hydrangeas were always that deep, vibrant blue because she buried rusty nails in the soil. 

But yes, to answer your question again, the voice and the watching were definitely there even when I wasn't feeling all sped up or depressed. Just a quiet spell, but they were still there.
Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs during the time these experiences have been happening?

Oh, goodness no. I don't touch any of that stuff. No drugs or drinking for me. I don't even like the smell of alcohol, honestly. It just smells sour, like yeast. 

You know what else smells exactly like that? That sourdough starter my Tuesday client, Mrs. Higgins, keeps right on her kitchen island. She treats that glass jar like it's a new puppy, feeding it flour every single day. I have to be so careful wiping the granite around it. One time, I accidentally bumped her flour canister while I was dusting the baker's rack next to it, and the lid wasn't on tight. It was that really fine pastry flour, and it just poofed everywhere, like a big white cloud. Took me nearly an hour to get it all out of the grout lines on her floor. 

She has that beautiful terracotta tile, imported from Spain, I think, and it's terribly porous. You can't use regular bleach on it or it ruins the finish entirely. You have to use a special pH-neutral stone cleaner. I have to buy it by the gallon at the janitorial supply store downtown. Parking down there is just a nightmare lately, though. They put in those new digital meters where you have to type in your license plate, and the screen is always too glaring in the sun to read what you're typing. I ended up getting a ticket last month because I typed a 'B' instead of an '8'. I tried to appeal it, but the city office puts you on hold for hours with this awful elevator music. 

But anyway, no, no drugs or alcohol for me. Never have.
During the time these experiences have been happening, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, everyone has a gloomy afternoon here and there, but not two whole weeks of just feeling sad all day. I honestly don't have the time to sit around feeling down in the dumps with my schedule. Thursdays especially are just back-to-back. I do the Henderson place in the morning, and let me tell you, they have this massive golden retriever named Barnaby. Sweetest dog, but the shedding is just out of control. 

I have to empty the vacuum canister three times just for their living room rug. I always tell my clients to get the bagged vacuums, the ones with the HEPA filters, because those bagless ones just puff dust right back in your face when you try to empty them into the trash can. And you have to be so careful with the outside trash bins at the Henderson's because they have raccoons terrible in that neighborhood. Big, fat ones that just sit on the fence and stare at you like they own the place. 

My neighbor, Mr. Gable, tried putting bungee cords over his trash lids to keep the raccoons out, but they just chewed right through the elastic. He ended up having to sprinkle cayenne pepper all over the bags. It works, I guess, but if the wind catches it when you're taking the recycling out, it gets right in your eyes. It burns like you wouldn't believe. I had to flush my eyes out with the garden hose once, and the water was freezing cold. 

But anyway, no, I haven't had any long stretches of feeling depressed like you're asking about. Just too busy for all that.

But I know for a fact that the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house. And they follow me on my cleaning routes, too. I clean houses over in the Heights—beautiful homes, really, mostly hardwood floors which I actually prefer because vacuuming those thick, heavy rugs just absolutely kills my lower back. target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a quieter spell for several weeks when I was sleeping more and not rushing around as much, but I still heard the voice by the kitchen window and believed the agency was watching us.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the psychotic symptoms (voice, belief of being watched) occurred for at least two weeks in the absence of any manic or depressive symptoms, which directly maps to Additional Requirement 3.

patient.answer:
I feel like we just talked about this, Doctor. Are you testing my memory? But yes, like I said before, there was a quieter spell for several weeks. I wasn't rushing around cleaning everything in sight, and I wasn't feeling down in the dumps either, you know? I was sleeping a lot more, actually. But even with all that calmness, I still heard that woman's voice right by the kitchen window, and I knew the agency was out there watching us. 

Speaking of sleeping more, I had to buy a new mattress pad because my old one got a tear right down the middle. I went to that big department store out by the highway, the one with the huge parking lot that always has those seagulls circling around. I don't know why seagulls hang out in parking lots so far from the ocean. They just sit on the light poles and squawk at people pushing their carts. I had a cart with a wonky wheel, of course. It kept pulling to the left, and I ended up bumping into a display of those scented pinecones they put out for the holidays. 

They smell so strong, those pinecones. Cinnamon and apple and I don't know what else. It gives me a terrible headache. I prefer natural scents, like lavender. I keep little sachets of dried lavender in my linen closet to keep the moths away. My grandmother taught me that. She used to grow huge bushes of it in her front yard, right next to the hydrangeas. Her hydrangeas were always that deep, vibrant blue because she buried rusty nails in the soil. 

But yes, to answer your question again, the voice and the watching were definitely there even when I wasn't feeling all sped up or depressed. Just a quiet spell, but they were still there.

inference.note: Reported manic symptoms and disorganized/loosely associated speech make schizophrenia less likely as the sole diagnosis, while persistent delusions and hallucinations outside mood episodes argue against a purely mood disorder.

doctor.intent: Clarify whether the psychotic symptoms are substance/medication-induced, which would separate a schizophrenia-spectrum disorder from substance/medication-related psychosis
doctor.question: Have you been using any alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs during the time these experiences have been happening?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about substance use (alcohol, cannabis, stimulants, or other drugs), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Oh, goodness no. I don't touch any of that stuff. No drugs or drinking for me. I don't even like the smell of alcohol, honestly. It just smells sour, like yeast. 

You know what else smells exactly like that? That sourdough starter my Tuesday client, Mrs. Higgins, keeps right on her kitchen island. She treats that glass jar like it's a new puppy, feeding it flour every single day. I have to be so careful wiping the granite around it. One time, I accidentally bumped her flour canister while I was dusting the baker's rack next to it, and the lid wasn't on tight. It was that really fine pastry flour, and it just poofed everywhere, like a big white cloud. Took me nearly an hour to get it all out of the grout lines on her floor. 

She has that beautiful terracotta tile, imported from Spain, I think, and it's terribly porous. You can't use regular bleach on it or it ruins the finish entirely. You have to use a special pH-neutral stone cleaner. I have to buy it by the gallon at the janitorial supply store downtown. Parking down there is just a nightmare lately, though. They put in those new digital meters where you have to type in your license plate, and the screen is always too glaring in the sun to read what you're typing. I ended up getting a ticket last month because I typed a 'B' instead of an '8'. I tried to appeal it, but the city office puts you on hold for hours with this awful elevator music. 

But anyway, no, no drugs or alcohol for me. Never have.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient has had a major depressive episode, which would separate schizoaffective disorder from delusional disorder.
doctor.question: During the time these experiences have been happening, have you had a period of at least two weeks when you felt depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about a major depressive episode, which is not part of my symptom profile since I have Schizoaffective Disorder, Bipolar Type, and my profile does not include depressive symptoms.

patient.answer:
Depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, everyone has a gloomy afternoon here and there, but not two whole weeks of just feeling sad all day. I honestly don't have the time to sit around feeling down in the dumps with my schedule. Thursdays especially are just back-to-back. I do the Henderson place in the morning, and let me tell you, they have this massive golden retriever named Barnaby. Sweetest dog, but the shedding is just out of control. 

I have to empty the vacuum canister three times just for their living room rug. I always tell my clients to get the bagged vacuums, the ones with the HEPA filters, because those bagless ones just puff dust right back in your face when you try to empty them into the trash can. And you have to be so careful with the outside trash bins at the Henderson's because they have raccoons terrible in that neighborhood. Big, fat ones that just sit on the fence and stare at you like they own the place. 

My neighbor, Mr. Gable, tried putting bungee cords over his trash lids to keep the raccoons out, but they just chewed right through the elastic. He ended up having to sprinkle cayenne pepper all over the bags. It works, I guess, but if the wind catches it when you're taking the recycling out, it gets right in your eyes. It burns like you wouldn't believe. I had to flush my eyes out with the garden hose once, and the water was freezing cold. 

But anyway, no, I haven't had any long stretches of feeling depressed like you're asking about. Just too busy for all that.

opening_question.intent: Open the interview and identify the main presenting complaint.
opening_question.question: Hello, I’m Dr. ___. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent persecutory delusions and auditory hallucinations for about 11 months, with at least several-week periods when these psychotic symptoms persisted despite euthymic mood and also outside of mood episodes. There is also clear mood pathology with a history suggestive of an elevated/activated period with decreased need for sleep, increased activity, and pressured/derailing speech, along with a quieter low-energy period. Because psychotic symptoms are present for a substantial portion of the illness but also occur independently of mood episodes, schizoaffective disorder, depressed type is the best fit among the candidates.
